text:
alex.k: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a tiny shim in each SDK to unify resume semantics for streaming+paged endpoints. Thoughts?

maria: tl;dr?

alex.k: Right now Python/TS/Go diverge on whether resume token is opaque (transport) or SDK-level cursor. I want a single contract so app code doesn't need per-lang special casing.

jun: agree we need consistency. do you mean the SDK should own the resume token format? or pass-through whatever the server gives?

alex.k: two options: 
1) pass-through: server issues opaque token, SDK threads it through on retry/resume. minimal SDK logic.
2) SDK-normalized: SDK exposes a small structured token (seq, offset, opaque) and maps to server tokens.

sam: option1 simpler. fewer surface area bugs. but option2 buys us nicer client features (prefetch, partial replays).

nicole: if SDK-normalized, how do we handle cross-region fallback where tokens are incompatible?
alex.k: we'd keep original opaque token as a fallback field. normalized token is a best-effort convenience. if server rejects normalized form we fall back to opaque.

maria: what about idempotency + retries? streaming resumption can re-run last N events. apps need guidance.
jun: recommend SDK emit an enum on resume: "approximate" vs "exact" vs "unsupported" so callers can decide to de-dupe.
sam: +1. docs should show small pattern: keep last-ack id and reconcile on resume.

nicole: language differences: Python has async iterators, TS has async generators, Go has blocking channels. How do we present the resume surface?
alex.k: API shape idea — keep minimal across langs: 
```
resume_token: string | null  # opaque for transport
resume_hint: string | null   # optional normalized hint (base64 json)
resume_quality: "exact" | "approximate" | "none"
```
SDK exposes all three. languages can map to idiomatic types (iterator state in Go, generator state in TS).

maria: That base64 JSON in resume_hint feels sticky. any perf concerns?
jun: it's tiny, usually <256 bytes. main cost is serializing on every item if we do automatic checkpointing. keep it cheap.

sam: Another trade: do retries/resume happen at transport layer (automatic) or require app opt-in?
alex.k: propose SDK-level policy: automatic short retry window (idempotent-only) + explicit resume APIs for non-idempotent flows. Default: transport retries for transient errors, but resume tokens only used when caller enabled checkpointing.
nicole: So e.g., embeddings/paged lists do automatic retry, but long-running streaming call needs explicit checkpoint.
jun: yes. and we should provide helpers: checkpoint_every(n_items) and checkpoint_on_time(ms). SDK handles token persistence.
maria: storage API for tokens? We shouldn't force a pattern. make it pluggable: in-memory default, and allow user to provide async callback to persist.
alex.k: agreed. signature: `persist(token: string) -> Promise<void>` / `load() -> Promise<string|null>` for TS/Python; Go uses interfaces.
sam: One sticky: how do we test cross-language interoperability? We need a test harness that issues tokens from reference server and asserts resume behavior on all SDKs.
jun: we can add a small interop CI job that uses the server test endpoint which returns weird tokens (mangled, region-bound) and ensure SDK falls back cleanly.
nicole: ops-bot: deploy windows? :smile:

ops-bot: @alex.k triggered interop-ci job: build/interop-resume-2026-03-21 started (job id 5642) :gear:

alex.k: Nice. One more edge: pagination + streaming hybrid (paged streaming windows). If user pages through, then switches to stream resume we should keep single resume contract. That argues for SDK-normalized token.
maria: but normalized token increases coupling to server semantics. need versioning field in token.
jun: include `v` and `origin` in hint. example `{"v":1,"origin":"inference-v2","cursor_seq":42}` then base64 it.
sam: Also recommend TTL for tokens. older tokens should error with clear 4xx code. SDK translate that to `ResumeStaleError` so caller can choose full resync.
nicole: telemetry: track how often we fall back to opaque vs normalized. helps server+SDK land on stable shape.
alex.k: good call. we'll add counters: resume.normalized_ok, resume.fallback_opaque, resume.stale_errors.

maria: docs needed: migration guide for users who currently stash raw tokens. show how to accept new normalized hint without breaking.
jun: implement plan:
- add small shim in each SDK for 1.0 (opt-in flag `enable_resume_hint=true`)
- interop CI tests against server combos
- Add telemetry + error mapping
- Docs + examples for Python/TS/Go

sam: timeline?
alex.k: prototyping this week, ship alpha in next minor release (2 weeks), flip opt-in by default after 6 weeks if interop stable.
nicole: :thumbsup:

alex.k: ok I'll open follow-up PRs for TS/Python/Go with the proposed signatures and link the interop CI job. thanks all for quick takes.

maria: thanks — really helps.

jun: will review PRs later today.

ops-bot: interop job 5642: build/interop-resume-2026-03-21 succeeded (:tada:)
